a: A pure function has no side effects and returns the same output for the same inputs.
Immutable data is never changed in place; updates create new values.
A higher-order function takes or returns functions (map, filter, reduce).
map transforms; filter selects; reduce aggregates a collection.
Currying turns a multi-arg function into a chain of single-arg functions.
Monads structure computations with context (Maybe, IO) via bind/return.
Lazy evaluation computes values only when needed.
An expression is referentially transparent if it can be replaced by its value safely.
Haskell, Elixir, and parts of Scala/F#/JS/Python support functional style.
